newsitem.title: USA: U.S. diplomat Lord to head for Tokyo and Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: U.S. diplomat Lord to head for Tokyo and Hong Kong.

text.p: Assistant Secretary of State Winston Lord will leave for Tokyo and Hong Kong on Saturday for meetings about U.S. troops on Okinawa and Hong Kong's transfer from Britain to China, the State Department said.

Lord, who accompanied President Bill Clinton on a 12-day trip to Asia that ended on Wednesday, will return to the region for a Dec. 1-3 meeting of the U.S.-Japanese security consultative committee, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

Defence Secretary William Perry, U.S. Ambassador to Japan Walter Mondale, Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda and Fumio Kyuma, director general of Japan's Defence Agency, will take part, Burns said at a briefing.
He said the "very important meeting" would review the final report of the joint committee set up to review problems caused by the stationing of U.S. troops on Okinawa.

Okinawans resent the noise, aircraft accidents and crime associated with the U.S. forces and in September they voted in favour of reducing the size of the contingent. Bases on the subtropical island account for about half the 47,000 U.S. service people in Japan.
The rape of an Okinawan schoolgirl by U.S. servicemen in 1995 heightened local opposition to the bases. Both Washington and Tokyo have stressed their commitment to responding to Okinawan concerns.

After the Tokyo talks, Burns said, Lord will travel to Hong Kong for meetings on Dec. 4 and 5 with Gov. Chris Patten, Chief Secretary Anson Chan and a variety of Hong Kong legislators, as well as the representative of China.

"In his meetings, Ambassador Lord will stress the United States' support for a smooth and successful transition and continued political and civil freedoms in Hong Kong after reversion" of the British colony to China in 1997, Burns said.
